order.title: Door lock that opens only for codes 0, 2, 7, 8, 9, 14, built from only NAND chips, at most 16
order.spec: A door lock with 4 switches a, b, c, d (a is the biggest digit of the binary number): the light y turns on only when the switches show the numbers 0, 2, 7, 8, 9 or 14, and stays off for every other number. Build it using only NAND chips (a NOT is a NAND with both inputs tied together) and at most 16 chips in total.

definition_of_done: Functional correctness: for all 16 possible input combinations of a,b,c,d, output y must be 1 exactly for inputs representing binary numbers 0, 2, 7, 8, 9, 14 (a is MSB), and 0 for all other inputs.
Gate count: total number of NAND gates (including NOT implemented as NAND with both inputs tied together) must not exceed 16.
Gate types: every gate in the blueprint must be of type NAND; NOT gates must be implemented strictly as a NAND gate with both inputs connected to the same signal.
Naming uniqueness: every gate must have a unique name; no name may be used for both a gate instance and a signal/output, and all gate names must be distinct across the entire blueprint.

Input/output connectivity: every gate must have exactly 1 or 2 inputs (for NAND gates, 2 inputs; for NOT, 2 inputs tied to the same signal) and exactly 1 output. Every gate output must drive exactly one gate input or the primary output y, with no floating or wire-OR connections.
Primary inputs: the blueprint must declare exactly four primary inputs named a, b, c, d, with a corresponding to the most significant bit of the 4-bit binary number.
Primary output: the blueprint must declare exactly one primary output named y.
Signal completeness: every gate input must be connected to either a primary input or another gate output; no input may be left unconnected or tied to an undefined signal.

Library part compliance: if any library part is referenced via the `reuse` field, its declared inputs and outputs must match the blueprint's port definitions exactly; in this design, no library parts are reused.
Inspector verification: the design must pass automated checking on all 16 input vectors by the AutoFab inspector, which does not trust claims and validates every gate and connection.
